title: Compressed insights — short reading digest on LLM efficiency
content:
Mini digest (short, actionable). Purpose: capture quick takeaways from 5 papers/blogs + conference notes and jot down small experiments to try on Redwood runtime. Keep lean — want items I can slot into a 2-4 hour experiment window.

1) Paper: 'Sparse-state attention for extended contexts' (arXiv summary)
- Core idea: selectively attend to a compressed scaffold of previous tokens instead of full KV every step; runtime savings scale with context length.
- Perf notes: lower memory bandwidth and lower KV lookups. Latency cost depends heavily on scaffold construction cost.
- Why it matters for us: if scaffold construction is cheap and can be cached across requests, could reduce per-token cost on very long contexts ( > 65k).
- Quick experiment: implement a crude scaffold builder on top of existing KV cache simulator, measure memory footprint & token generation latency for 32k and 128k contexts. Hypothesis: >2x mem reduction, ~1.1x latency overhead for reconstruct.

2) Blog: 'Quant-aware fine-tuning for 4-bit models'
- Summary: fine-tune with simulated quant noise, then export weights with scale-aware packing yields surprisingly small quality loss.
- Observations: some layers are fragile (ffn1/attn_proj). Need per-layer learning rate multipliers.
- For Redwood: combine with our Optimize suggestions to detect fragility and recommend partial fine-tuning profiles when customers want ultra-low-bit deploys.
- To try: take a tuned 7B model, do 1k-step quant-aware fine-tune on small instruction dataset and run our eval harness to compare helpfulness/toxicity tradeoffs.

3) Conference takeaways: 'KV compression lightning talks' (notes from workshop)
- Many teams favor blockwise compression with occasional full-refreshes rather than continuous lossy compaction.
- Practical tip: maintain two-tier cache: recent exact KVs + older compressed summaries. Eviction policy should be workload aware (retrieval-heavy vs. chat-handoff).
- Implementation note: need a fast decompress kernel — compress/decompress latency must be < 0.5ms per token to be helpful at low latency SLOs.

4) Systems paper: 'Latency vs. Batching tradeoffs in production'
- Key metric: 95th percentile cost-per-token when varying batch time windows. Small windows kill GPU utilization but keep tail latency low. Larger windows improve cost but push 95/99p higher.
- Redwood angle: dynamic batching policies that adapt to real-time load shape can sit on the Pareto frontier. Idea: use short microwindows for premium customers and longer windows for low-tier; or use predictive batching when request rate is predictable.
- Quick test: simulate traffic traces (spiky startup app + steady background) and run our batching simulator to estimate cost delta.

5) Short note: 'Evaluation heuristics for quantized regressions'
- Don't rely solely on token-level perplexity. Use small targeted evals: instruction divergence, extraction accuracy (span F1), and safety probes. Some quantization schemes hallucinate more on extraction tasks even though perplexity looks fine.
- Action: extend our Optimize eval templates to include extraction and instruction-fast-fail tests.

Notes to self / practical action items (slot into next two weeks):
- A: Lightweight scaffold experiment (4-6 hours): implement compressed-scaffold KV approach in the local KV sim. Measure mem & wall-clock for 32k/64k/128k contexts. (owner: me)
- B: Quant-aware fine-tune smoke (8-12 hours): pick 7B open model, run 1k steps of quant-aware tuning, run 3 eval prompts from Optimize suite. (owner: me + Ava)
- C: Batching simulation (6 hours): use 3 synthetic traces and compare static vs adaptive policies; produce a short graph for next eng sync. (owner: Ethan)
- D: Add two extraction tests to Optimize eval harness and run for baseline models (2-3 hours).

Open questions / risks:
- How much engineering complexity is acceptable for scaffold caching vs. gains? If scaffold build is expensive per request, wins evaporate.
- Compatibility across model variants (dense -> sparse, different vocab/tokenizers) — need to ensure scaffold concept generalizes.
- For quant-aware tuning, customer expectations: will we offer as 'recommended profile' or gate behind Dedicated + private?

Cross refs / quick links for follow-up:
- PR-4821 contains initial KV cache simulator changes (internal).
- Jira CON-2026-77 is workshop follow-up for KV compression experiments.
- Slack: #kv-compression thread (search: "scaffold approach")

Final micro-summary (one line each):
- Scaffold idea: good memory win for extreme context but questionable per-request overhead unless cached.
- Quant-aware FT: promising for 4-bit deployments; needs careful per-layer tuning.
- KV two-tier cache: practical and incremental to implement.
- Batching policy: adaptive policies can trade cost vs. tail latency cleanly for multi-tenant.

If I get time this week: run scaffold sim and one quant-aware smoke. Otherwise, move one smaller TODO to next sprint.
